titleEn: When Chickens Go to Bed, I Go Home!

pages.text: "I'm not going! Just one more stone!" Mumu stacked stones under the well tree. The sun slipped behind it, and the road grew dark. Mumu held back a yawn.
"Taro, let's play a little longer. Just up to ten!" Mumu tugged his hand. Quick-handed monkey Taro had finished his stack already. "It's getting dark..." He looked across the road.
A stone slipped from Mumu's hand. The tower tumbled sideways and scattered. "Oh...? The stones keep slipping." Mumu's eyes were half closed.
One by one, chickens climbed onto a branch. Cluck, cluck. Mumu turned their ears toward them. "The chickens are going to bed, too," Taro said.
"When chickens climb onto their branch, it's evening." Taro pointed to both sides of the road. A lamp glowed in each house. He sang, "When Chickens Go to Bed, I Go Home!"
Mumu laid the remaining stones side by side under the tree. "Let's start here again tomorrow." Taro pointed to the spot. Mumu's hands felt light.
They waved in the middle of the road. Mumu bounded toward their own lamp; Taro trotted toward the lamp across the road. "When Chickens Go to Bed, I Go Home!"

Mumu lay down in the room. Beyond the threshold, empty leaf plates sat on the porch. Outside was quiet. The chickens and village were all asleep. "Taro must be lying down now, too." Mumu closed their eyes.
The next evening, Mumu put down the stones and stood up first. "One, stop when chickens climb onto their branch! Two, put down what I'm holding! Three, go home!" Still seated, Taro looked up.

In the morning, Taro jumped up and hung around Mumu's neck. Going home to sleep with the chickens meant they could meet and play again in the morning. Mumu bounded up and called, "When Chickens Go to Bed, I Go Home!"
